customManagers.description: The structurizr.war the `structurizr` CI job runs, pinned by STRUCTURIZR_VERSION under a `# renovate:` comment. Structurizr tags its application releases `vYYYY.MM.DD` and its library releases `vX.Y.Z` in the same repository; the regex versioning keeps only the dated ones. A new WAR can change what `pnpm fixtures:acceptance` writes, and then the job fails until the pull request commits the regenerated fixture.

The Mermaid release the build's Mermaid reader is generated from, pinned by MERMAID_VERSION under a `// renovate:` comment in scripts/mermaid/generate/index.js. `mermaid` is never a dependency of Renderizr (ADR 24), so the npm manager never sees it. Renovate can't run the generator: its pull request changes only the pin, and needs `pnpm mermaid:parser` run and the regenerated scripts/mermaid/parser.js committed before it merges.

packageRules.description: Keep the pinned action digests current. Every third-party action in .github/workflows is pinned to a full commit SHA for OpenSSF Scorecard's Pinned-Dependencies check; without this rule those pins rot into a security liability instead of being one. One PR, monthly, since they move together and none of them ship into user output.

packageRules.description: Development tooling: lint, types, commit plumbing, property tests. None of it reaches a rendered workspace, so one grouped PR per week is enough review surface.

The rendering runtime. These are the packages whose code is inlined into the page a user publishes, so each one gets its own PR (React and React DOM, which must match, share one), which keeps a bad update easy to find and revert — never grouped, never rolled up with anything else. Their commits use `fix(deps)`, so release-please prepares a patch release for each one. An update that changes what users publish reaches them only through a release, and release-please releases nothing for the `chore` type every other update uses.

React and React DOM update together, in one PR. React DOM refuses to run against a React of any other version, so a PR that moves only one of them leaves a lockfile that cannot draw a page, and CI fails on both PRs until a person merges them by hand. The rule above sets `groupName` to null, which also drops the React monorepo group `config:recommended` brings, so this rule puts it back for the two packages that ship.

@dagrejs/* is pinned to exact versions in package.json on purpose: `src/engine/layout/dagre-order.ts` ports Dagre's internal `lib/order` modules from the pinned version, and those carry no semver promise. Renovate replaces the exact version with a new exact version; it must never widen the pin into a range.
`engines` states the supported Node and pnpm range — a compatibility promise made in README.md and enforced by the CI matrix. Raising it is a decision, not a dependency update.

Auto-merge every patch, minor, pin and digest update, for npm and GitHub Actions alike, runtime packages included. CI is the review: nothing merges without the `ci` check, which runs the whole suite and both render modes, and `minimumReleaseAge` keeps anything from merging the day it is published (14 days for @dagrejs/*). Majors and lock file maintenance stay manual: a major changes APIs and behavior, and those pull requests still need a person.

Never auto-merge a new Mermaid pin: the pull request only moves MERMAID_VERSION, and CI passes on the parser generated from the old one. A person runs `pnpm mermaid:parser`, commits scripts/mermaid/parser.js and checks the Mermaid fixtures before it merges.
